core_obligations: Observe that the product prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(x)) is monic with coefficients fixed by every element of G, hence lies in R^G[T] (proof line 32577).

Reduce the general case x = f_1 b_1 + ... + f_m b_m with f_j in J and b_j in R to the single-step case x = y - fb with f in J, b in R and y in JR already handled, by induction on m (proof lines 32578-32580).
Expand prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(y) + f sigma(b)) as the polynomial for y plus a sum of terms f^i a_i, and read off the explicit subset-sum expression for a_i (proof lines 32583-32594).
Show a_i lies in R^G by the symmetry of that expression, and conclude that the polynomial for x is congruent modulo J to the polynomial for y, which is the induction step (proof lines 32595-32599).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a finite group G of order n acting on a ring R, an ideal J of the invariant subring R^G, and an element x in the extended ideal JR (source lines 32568-32574). The proof has to reduce a general presentation x = f_1 b_1 + ... + f_m b_m with f_j in J to the one-step shape x = y - fb (proof lines 32578-32580), then compare the two monic polynomials prod (T - sigma(x)) and prod (T - sigma(y)) coefficient by coefficient (proof lines 32583-32587), and it must show that each auxiliary coefficient a_i, written as a sum over i-element subsets of G, actually lies in the invariant ring R^G (proof lines 32590-32595). The non-routine part is that invariance step together with the congruence modulo J that makes the induction go through; only the symmetry of the displayed expression is cited, and that computation is omitted by the author.
